summary: build() writes d_ilist on the device but never calls k_list->k_ilist.modify<DeviceType>(), so a later k_ilist.sync_host() is a no-op and consumers read stale host ilist data.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:151 'd_ilist(inum) = i;' (device kernel) and the end of build() at :97-105 has no modify call.  Every other KOKKOS npair build does it: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:360 'list->k_ilist.template modify<DeviceType>();', src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:82, src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:520, src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:84.  Consumers rely on the flag: src/KOKKOS/npair_copy_kokkos.cpp:77 and src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:130 call 'listcopy_kk->k_ilist.sync_host()' before reading view_host(), as does src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_species_kokkos.cpp:80.
failure_scenario: A CPU-side list copied or trimmed from a skip/kk/device list (kk2cpu path in NPairCopyKokkos::copy_to_cpu / NPairTrimKokkos::trim_to_cpu), or fix reaxff/species, reads the host mirror of k_ilist, which still contains whatever the last host-side write left (all zeros on the first build) -> wrong atom indices, wrong neighbor lists, likely out-of-bounds firstneigh entries.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_list->k_ilist.template modify<DeviceType>();' at the end of NPairSkipKokkos::build(), as the sibling npair styles do.

summary: The TRIM branch drops the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype] when the skip list's own request has no custom cutoff.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:50 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and :144 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;' vs src/npair_skip.cpp:108-109 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  Note src/neighbor.cpp:1244-1252 clears ->cut for skip requests ('skip lists inherit the cutoff of the parent they skip from'), so cutoff_custom is 0 for exactly the skip lists this class builds.
failure_scenario: A skip/trim/kk/* list whose request had its ->cut flag cleared by morph_unique() has cutoff_custom == 0, so every neighbor fails 'rsq > 0.0' and the sub-style's neighbor list is empty; the CPU build of the same input trims to the per-type neighbor cutoffs instead.
suggested_fix: Use the same '(cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]' rule, with cutneighsq mirrored into a device view.

summary: The KOKKOS skip build ignores list->molskip entirely and unconditionally dereferences list->iskip / list->ijskip, which are left as null pointers for molecular skip lists.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:75-79 'k_iskip.view_host()(itype) = list->iskip[itype]; ... k_ijskip.view_host()(itype,jtype) = list->ijskip[itype][jtype];' and the kernel at :122 'if (!d_iskip(itype))' / :137 'if (d_ijskip(itype,type(j))) continue;'.  src/neigh_list.cpp:159-171 only allocates iskip/ijskip when '!molskip'.  The CPU base src/npair_skip.cpp:51,78,98-100 reads 'int molskip = list->molskip;' and applies 'if (!molskip && iskip[itype]) continue;' plus the INTRA/INTER molecule tests; the INTEL variant does the same (src/INTEL/npair_skip_intel.cpp:117,149-151).
failure_scenario: pair_style hybrid/molecular (the only setter, src/pair_hybrid_molecular.cpp:48,51) with a KOKKOS sub-style produces a skip list with molskip != 0 and iskip == ijskip == nullptr; NPairSkipKokkos::build() dereferences the null pointers at :76/:78 -> segmentation fault (and even if they were allocated the intra/inter-molecular filtering would be missing).
suggested_fix: Port the molskip logic (sync MOLECULE_MASK, pass atom->molecule into the functor, apply the INTRA/INTER tests) and skip the iskip/ijskip fill when list->molskip is set; alternatively error out for molskip lists in the KOKKOS skip builder.

summary: d_inum is only written by the thread handling ii == num_skip-1, so when num_skip is 0 the previous build's inum is reused for list->inum.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:157-160 'if (final) { if (ii == num_skip-1) d_inum() = inum; }' - with num_skip == 0 the RangePolicy(0,0) runs no iterations, yet :94-97 still reads d_inum into list->inum.  The CPU base src/npair_skip.cpp:62,122 starts from 'int inum = 0;' and always assigns 'list->inum = inum;'.
failure_scenario: A processor whose parent skip list becomes empty (all atoms migrated away) keeps the stale, larger inum from the previous build; consumers then iterate d_ilist beyond the valid range.
suggested_fix: Deep-copy 0 into d_inum before the parallel_scan, or set list->inum = 0 explicitly when num_skip == 0.

summary: NPairSkipKokkos::build() writes d_ilist in a device kernel but never claims k_ilist.modify<DeviceType>(), so the later k_ilist.sync_host() done by NPairCopyKokkos/NPairTrimKokkos/fix reaxff/species is a no-op and those consumers read a stale host ilist.
verified_by: orchestrator (end of build() at src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:90-104 has no modify call; every sibling has one - npair_kokkos.cpp:360, npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:82, npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:84, npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:520).

summary: AtomKokkos::map_set_device() reallocates sametag BEFORE the map_init(0) call that may free it, so for MAP_HASH the kernel writes into a destroyed, zero-extent k_sametag view.
failure_scenario: Run with the Kokkos device atom map (default, kokkos atom/map not legacy) and atom_modify map hash (or >1e6 atom IDs so hash is auto-selected).  When this rank's nlocal+nghost grows past map_nhash (load imbalance, ghost growth), map_init(0) recreates the hash, which calls map_delete() and destroys k_sametag / sets max_same=0.  The following parallel_for then writes d_sametag(i) for i in [0,nall) into a zero-extent view: out-of-bounds device write / memory corruption (Kokkos bounds-check abort in a debug build), and k_sametag.sync_host() at line 267 leaves sametag == nullptr for all later host users (Domain::closest_image, Special).
suggested_fix: Move the 'if (nall > max_same) {...}' sametag (re)allocation block below the 'if (map_style == MAP_HASH) { if (nall > map_nhash) map_init(0); }' block, matching src/atom_map.cpp:196-201 and AtomKokkos::map_set_host().

summary: map_one() sets the hash dual view's modified_host flag, and the next device-side map_clear()/map_set_device() calls modify_device() while that flag is still set, which dual_hash_type turns into an unconditional Kokkos::abort("Concurrent modification of host and device hashes").
evidence: atom_map_kokkos.cpp:396-404 map_one hash branch: sync_host(); insert; k_map_hash.modify_host(). atom_map_kokkos.cpp:139-147 map_clear hash branch with atom_map_legacy==0: view_device().clear(); k_map_hash.modify_device(). atom_map_kokkos.cpp:54-66 map_init(check=0) with !recreate and atom_map_legacy==0 calls map_clear(). atom_map_kokkos.cpp:272 map_set_device ends with k_map_hash.modify_device(). kokkos_type.h:650-662 modify_device()/modify_host() abort when both flags are set; only sync_host()/sync_device() clear a flag. kokkos.cpp:355 sets atom_map_legacy = 0 whenever ngpus > 0. special.cpp:658-746 does map_clear(); map_one() x N; map_init(0); map_set().
failure_scenario: GPU run (default package kokkos atom/map device) with atom_modify map hash (or auto-selected hash for > 1M tags) on any molecular system: Special::build() -> map_clear [modify_device] -> map_one [sync_host clears device flag, sets host flag] -> map_init(0) [hash not grown -> map_clear -> modify_device with host flag set] -> abort. Same sequence in FixShake rendezvous and in Special::onefive_build/fix_bond_create paths.
suggested_fix: In the device branches of map_clear() and map_set_device(), release the host state before claiming the device (e.g. add a clear_sync_state()/reset to dual_hash_type, or call sync_device() first), mirroring k_map_array.clear_sync_state() at line 131.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 06)
summary: map_set_device() reallocates k_sametag BEFORE the map_init(0) call that can invoke map_delete() and destroy it, so with MAP_HASH a hash regrow leaves the kernel writing sametag into a destroyed zero-extent view; the comment in the code even says the reallocation must come after map_init().
evidence: atom_map_kokkos.cpp:173-192 (sametag realloc at 178-182, then 'possible reallocation of sametag must come after map_init()' comment and map_init(0) at 184-192). CPU src/atom_map.cpp does map_init(0) first, then the sametag realloc. map_set_host() (atom_map_kokkos.cpp:290-294 region) has the correct order.
failure_scenario: Device atom map + hash map: when nlocal+nghost on a rank grows past map_nhash, map_init(0) recreates the map via map_delete() (destroys k_sametag, max_same=0); the subsequent parallel_for writes d_sametag(i) into a zero-extent view -> out-of-bounds device write / bounds-check abort, and sametag stays nullptr for later host users.
suggested_fix: Move the 'if (nall > max_same) {...}' block below the MAP_HASH map_init(0) block, as in src/atom_map.cpp and map_set_host().

summary: FixGravityKokkos::post_force() ignores the 'disable' keyword and applies the gravitational force even when the user asked for it to be disabled.
failure_scenario: 'fix g all gravity/kk 1.0 vector 0 0 -1 disable' (used together with granular pair styles that only extract gvec) applies a full gravitational force on every atom every step instead of none; total energy/trajectory is wrong versus the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (disable) return;' after the varflag block (before the atomKK->sync call) in FixGravityKokkos::post_force(), matching src/fix_gravity.cpp:276.

summary: FixGravityKokkos::post_force() has no 'if (disable) return;' guard, so 'fix gravity/kk ... disable' still applies the gravitational force.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/fix_gravity.cpp:274-276 returns early on disable; grep 'disable' over src/KOKKOS/fix_gravity_kokkos.cpp returns nothing).

summary: fix gravity/kk reads per-type mass on the device without syncing atomKK->k_mass.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_gravity_kokkos.cpp:66-69 `if (atomKK->rmass) rmass = ...; else mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();` and the kernel at line 113 `KK_FLOAT massone = mass[type[i]];`.  The only sync in the whole file is `atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read)` at line 61, and no mask bit exists for mass (src/atom_masks.h has no MASS_MASK); `grep -n 'k_mass' fix_gravity_kokkos.cpp` shows no `sync<DeviceType>()`.  Compare src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46, which does `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` in init().
failure_scenario: GPU run with per-type masses where no other KOKKOS style has synced k_mass (or where a `mass` command after the last sync re-marked the host copy newer): d_mass is zero/stale, so the gravitational force `massone*xacc` is zero (or wrong) and the reported gravitational potential energy is wrong.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: angle_style hybrid/kk dereferences a null cvatom of its sub-styles because it keeps the inherited centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL while every KOKKOS angle sub-style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:144-150 'if (cvflag_atom) { int n = atom->nlocal; ... double **cvatom_substyle = styles[m]->cvatom; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) for (int j = 0; j < 9; j++) cvatom[i][j] += cvatom_substyle[i][j]; }'. AngleHybridKokkos's constructor (src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:33-44) never touches centroidstressflag, and neither does src/angle_hybrid.cpp, so it keeps Angle's default 'centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL' (src/angle.cpp:48). Angle::ev_setup then sets 'cvflag_atom = 1' for the hybrid (src/angle.cpp:128). Every KOKKOS angle sub-style, however, sets 'centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL' in its constructor (e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:48, angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:48, angle_quartic_kokkos.cpp:44, angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:53, angle_table_kokkos.cpp:49, angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:42), so in their ev_setup src/angle.cpp:126-128 takes the 'vflag_atom = 1 / cvflag_atom = 0' branch and their 'cvatom' is never allocated (it stays the nullptr set in Angle's constructor). No CPU angle style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL (grep over src/**/angle_*.cpp returns only KOKKOS files), which is why the CPU angle_hybrid never hits this. PairHybrid does recompute the flag from its sub-styles (src/pair_hybrid.cpp:445-457); AngleHybrid/AngleHybridKokkos do not.
failure_scenario: angle_style hybrid/kk harmonic quartic (or any pair of kk angle styles) together with 'compute centroid/stress/atom' -> the run's ev_set() adds VIRIAL_CENTROID, AngleHybridKokkos::compute sets cvflag_atom = 1, the sub-style leaves cvatom == nullptr, and the accumulation loop segfaults on the first timestep. Even if it did not crash, the per-atom virial the sub-styles wrote into vatom would be silently discarded because the hybrid's own vflag_atom is 0.
suggested_fix: In AngleHybridKokkos::init_style() (after AngleHybrid::init_style()) recompute centroidstressflag from the sub-styles exactly as PairHybrid::init_one does (src/pair_hybrid.cpp:450-457): set CENTROID_NOTAVAIL if any sub-style is CENTROID_NOTAVAIL. Better still, add that loop to the CPU AngleHybrid so all hybrids inherit it.

summary: AngleHybridKokkos::maxangle_all is never initialised, so memory_usage() reads an indeterminate value if it is called before the first re-neighbour step.
evidence: 'int maxangle_all;' is declared at src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.h:43 and is written only inside the 'if (neighbor->ago == 0)' block, src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:85-88 ('maxangle_all = 0; for (int m = 0; m < nstyles; m++) if (h_nanglelist[m] > maxangle_all) maxangle_all = h_nanglelist[m] + EXTRA;'). The constructor (lines 33-44) and allocate() (lines 161-171) do not set it, while memory_usage() reads it at line 220: 'for (int m = 0; m < nstyles; m++) bytes += (double) maxangle_all * 4 * sizeof(int);'. The CPU class initialises the corresponding per-style array in allocate() ('for (int m = 0; m < nstyles; m++) maxangle[m] = 0;', src/angle_hybrid.cpp:161-166).
failure_scenario: 'angle_style hybrid/kk ... ; angle_coeff ... ; info coeffs' (or any memory_usage query issued before a run) reads uninitialised memory and prints a garbage or negative memory figure; it is undefined behaviour reported by valgrind/MSan.
suggested_fix: Initialise maxangle_all = 0 in the AngleHybridKokkos constructor (and/or in allocate()).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 01
summary: angle hybrid/kk never sets centroidstressflag (keeps CENTROID_AVAIL) while every kk angle sub-style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL, so with compute centroid/stress/atom the hybrid's cvflag_atom accumulation dereferences the sub-styles' null cvatom. Same shape confirmed by agents in dihedral_hybrid_kokkos (and to check in improper_hybrid_kokkos).
evidence: angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp constructor (33-44) and file contain no centroidstressflag; sub-styles e.g. angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:48 set CENTROID_NOTAVAIL; src/angle.cpp ev_setup sets cvflag_atom only when CENTROID_AVAIL.
failure_scenario: angle_style hybrid/kk + compute centroid/stress/atom: segfault in the cvatom accumulation loop on the first step.
suggested_fix: Derive centroidstressflag from the sub-styles in init_style() (as PairHybrid::init_one does) or set CENTROID_NOTAVAIL in the kk hybrid constructors.

summary: unpack_3d_permute1_n_functor multiplies the fast-index plane stride by nqty ('nqty*fast*nstride_plane'), but the CPU reference src/pack.h advances the destination index by exactly nstride_plane per fast index, so for nqty > 2 the unpack scatters data to wrong (and out-of-range) locations.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h:302-305: 'const int instart = plane + nqty*mid; int in = instart + nqty*fast*nstride_plane; int out = out_orig + nqty*mid*nfast + nqty*fast; for (int iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) d_data[data_offset + in++] = d_buf[buf_offset + out++];'. src/pack.h:175-179 (unpack_3d_permute1_n): 'instart = plane + nqty * mid; for (fast = 0; fast < nfast; fast++, instart += nstride_plane) { in = instart; for (iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) data[in++] = buf[out++]; }' -- i.e. the destination index is plane + nqty*mid + fast*nstride_plane, with NO nqty factor on the stride (nstride_plane is already in units of scalars, remap_kokkos.cpp:524 sets 'nstride_plane = nqty*out.ksize*out.jsize'). The nqty==2 sibling in the same file confirms the correct form: pack_kokkos.h:245 'const int in = in_orig + fast*nstride_plane;' (no factor 2). The buf index 'out' is computed correctly.
failure_scenario: A remap plan created with permute==1 and nqty>=3 (remap_kokkos.cpp:436-437 selects unpack_3d_permute1_n) writes each fast plane nqty times too far apart: with nqty=3 the last plane lands at 3*(nfast-1)*nstride_plane, roughly three times past the end of the receive brick -> silently corrupted FFT/remap output or an out-of-bounds device write. Currently latent: every in-tree caller uses nqty=1 (pppm_kokkos.cpp:891) or nqty=2 (fft3d_kokkos.cpp:473,498,539,567), so the _n variants are never selected today.
suggested_fix: Drop the nqty factor: 'int in = instart + fast*nstride_plane;' (and the same in unpack_3d_permute2_n_functor).

summary: unpack_3d_permute2_n_functor has the same defect as the permute1_n variant: it multiplies the fast-index line stride by nqty ('nqty*fast*nstride_line') where src/pack.h advances by nstride_line only.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h:466-469: 'const int instart = nqty*slow + mid*nstride_plane; int in = instart + nqty*fast*nstride_line; int out = out_orig + nqty*mid*nfast + nqty*fast;'. src/pack.h:257-261 (unpack_3d_permute2_n): 'instart = nqty * slow + mid * nstride_plane; for (fast = 0; fast < nfast; fast++, instart += nstride_line) { in = instart; for (iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) data[in++] = buf[out++]; }' -- destination index is nqty*slow + mid*nstride_plane + fast*nstride_line. The nqty==2 sibling pack_kokkos.h:411 'const int in = in_orig + fast*nstride_line;' has no factor 2, confirming the intended form.
failure_scenario: Same as the permute1_n case: a remap with permute==2 and nqty>=3 (remap_kokkos.cpp:444-445) scatters the unpacked values nqty times too far apart, corrupting the output brick or writing out of bounds. Latent today because no in-tree caller uses nqty>2.
suggested_fix: Change to 'int in = instart + fast*nstride_line;'.

summary: All eight pack/unpack functors decompose the flat Kokkos index so that the SLOW index varies fastest across threads, giving fully uncoalesced device loads and stores in every FFT remap.
evidence: pack_kokkos.h:73-76 (and identically at 128-131, 184-187, 238-241, 296-299, 351-354, 405-408, 461-464): 'const int fast = index / (nslow * nmid); const int index_new = index - (fast * nslow * nmid); const int mid = index_new / nslow; const int slow = index_new % nslow;'. Consecutive Kokkos indices therefore differ in 'slow', and the addresses used are 'd_buf[in_orig + mid*nfast + fast]' with in_orig = slow*nmid*nfast and 'd_data[plane + mid*nstride_line + fast]' with plane = slow*nstride_plane (line 77-82): adjacent threads are nmid*nfast resp. nstride_plane elements apart. The contiguous direction is 'fast' (src/pack.h:71 'for (fast = 0; ...) buf[in++] = data[out++]'), which here is the SLOWEST-varying thread index.
failure_scenario: No wrong results. On a GPU backend every remap in every 3d FFT (4 remaps per FFT, several FFTs per PPPM step) runs at a fraction of the achievable bandwidth because neither the read nor the write is coalesced.
suggested_fix: Swap the decomposition so 'fast' is the fastest-varying index (slow = index/(nmid*nfast); mid = (index/nfast)%nmid; fast = index%nfast), or use an MDRangePolicy with the fast index innermost.

summary: pack_kokkos.h has no include guard and includes the guard-less src/pack.h purely for 'struct pack_plan_3d', dragging ten unused static host functions into every translation unit that includes it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h has no '#ifndef LMP_PACK_KOKKOS_H'; line 18 '#include "pack.h"'. src/pack.h likewise has no include guard and, under the default FFT_PACK_ARRAY (pack.h:25-27), defines pack_3d, unpack_3d and the six unpack_3d_permute* functions as file-static (pack.h:55-264). Including either header twice in one translation unit is a redefinition error; today only src/KOKKOS/remap_kokkos.cpp includes pack_kokkos.h, so this is latent.
failure_scenario: A future file including pack_kokkos.h together with pack.h (or including pack_kokkos.h twice through another header) fails to compile; meanwhile every build emits unused-static-function warnings for the ten CPU pack routines.
suggested_fix: Add '#ifndef LMP_PACK_KOKKOS_H' guards to both headers, and move 'struct pack_plan_3d' into its own small header (or forward-declare it) so pack_kokkos.h does not pull in the CPU implementations.

summary: Same defect as pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos: the DSF self-energy is summed on the host from `atom->q[i]` while compute() only syncs q to the device, so on a GPU build the charges are stale after any device-side exchange or atom sort.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run with `pair_style born/coul/dsf/cs/kk`: after the first atom migration the host q array no longer matches the current local atoms, so the self-energy contribution to eng_coul (and to eatom) uses the wrong charges.
suggested_fix: Compute the self-energy inside the device kernel from the `q` device view (pattern of pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:228-236), or sync Q_MASK to the host first and loop over list->ilist.

summary: The core/shell EPSILON=1e-20 guard overflows in a single-precision KOKKOS build: r6inv = (1/EPSILON)^3 becomes inf in float, so a coincident core/shell pair produces NaN forces instead of a value the zero special-bond factor can cancel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_cs_kokkos.cpp:37 `static constexpr double EPSILON = 1.0e-20;`, :185 `const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPSILON);`, :187-196 `r2inv = 1.0/rsq; r6inv = r2inv*r2inv*r2inv; ... forceborn = born1*r*rexp - born2*r6inv + born3*r2inv*r6inv;`.  With LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE / SINGLE_DOUBLE (kokkos_type.h:400-408 make KK_FLOAT = float) and rsq_in == 0: r2inv = 1e20f, r2inv*r2inv already overflows float (max 3.4e38) to inf, so forceborn = -inf + inf = NaN and `factor_lj*NaN` stays NaN even for factor_lj == 0.  In the CPU style (src/CORESHELL/pair_born_coul_dsf_cs.cpp:104-124) everything is double and 1e60/1e80 stay finite, so the special-bond factor cancels them.  Same shape in pair_born_coul_wolf_cs_kokkos.cpp:190 and (pre-existing) pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:200.
failure_scenario: Single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, core/shell model where a shell starts exactly on its core (r == 0, the case EPSILON exists for) -> NaN pair forces on that pair.
suggested_fix: Do the EPSILON-guarded arithmetic in double (or use a larger, float-safe EPSILON such as 1e-12) in the CS kernels.

summary: The KOKKOS constructor re-creates all of the base class's plain arrays as dual views without first freeing the base allocations, orphaning ~4 MB per MPI rank (12 arrays: g_axis, the four cmap grids, num_crossterm and the six crossterm_* arrays).
evidence: src/MOLECULE/fix_cmap.cpp:94-98 allocates `g_axis`, `cmapgrid`, `d1cmapgrid`, `d2cmapgrid`, `d12cmapgrid` with memory->create, and line 116 `FixCMAP::grow_arrays(atom->nmax)` allocates `num_crossterm` and `crossterm_type`/`crossterm_atom1..5` with memory->grow. src/KOKKOS/fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp:57-61 then calls `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_g_axis,g_axis,...)` etc. and line 82 calls `FixCMAPKokkos::grow_arrays(atom->nmax)` -> `memoryKK->grow_kokkos(...)`, with no `memory->destroy(...)` in between. memory_kokkos.h:69-76 `grow_kokkos` for a 1d array does `array = data.view_host().data();` (the old pointer is simply dropped), and memory_kokkos.h:223-242 for a 2d array only `srealloc`s the row-pointer block, so the base's contiguous data block (the old `array[0]`) is leaked. Compare fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:125-126 and fix_acks2_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:93-94, which both call `memory->destroy(...)` immediately before handing the pointer to the KOKKOS allocator.
failure_scenario: Any `fix cmap/kk` run leaks 5 grid arrays (~110 KB) plus nmax*(4 + 6*4 + 5*6*8) bytes of per-atom arrays -- about 4.4 MB per rank at nmax = 16384 -- for the lifetime of the process; repeated fix/unfix or `clear` cycles accumulate it, and leak checkers in CI will flag it.
suggested_fix: Add `memory->destroy(g_axis); memory->destroy(cmapgrid); memory->destroy(d1cmapgrid); memory->destroy(d2cmapgrid); memory->destroy(d12cmapgrid);` before line 57 and `memory->destroy(num_crossterm); memory->destroy(crossterm_type); memory->destroy(crossterm_atom1..5);` before the grow_arrays() call at line 82.

summary: The bounds guard on the crossterm list uses `>` where `>=` is needed, so an index equal to maxcrossterm would be written one element past the end of d_crosstermlist.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp:212 `if (l_ncrosstermlist > maxcrossterm) Kokkos::abort("l_ncrosstermlist > maxcrossterm");` followed at 214-219 by `d_crosstermlist(l_ncrosstermlist,0..5) = ...`. d_crosstermlist is allocated with exactly `maxcrossterm` rows at line 158 (`memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_crosstermlist,maxcrossterm,CMAPMAX,...)`), so the valid range is 0..maxcrossterm-1. The CPU base uses the correct comparison, src/MOLECULE/fix_cmap.cpp:279 `if (ncrosstermlist == maxcrossterm) { maxcrossterm += LISTDELTA; ... }`. Additionally the check runs before the `if(is_final)` branch, where in the non-final scan pass `l_ncrosstermlist` is only a per-thread partial offset, so it does not reliably guard anything.
failure_scenario: A rank whose local crossterm count reaches maxcrossterm (= ncmap) writes six ints past the end of d_crosstermlist without tripping the guard. Reaching that count requires one rank to own every crossterm in the system, so this is a latent rather than routinely-hit overflow.
suggested_fix: Change the comparison to `>=` and move it inside the `if (is_final)` branch so it tests the actual write index.

summary: The per-atom energy/virial arrays are registered with the memory tag 'improper:eatom'/'improper:vatom' inside an angle style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:77 `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"improper:eatom");` and :84 `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_vatom,vatom,maxvatom,"improper:vatom");`. Every sibling uses the correct tag, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:76,81 `"angle:eatom"`, `"angle:vatom"`, matching the CPU base src/angle.cpp:137,144 ("angle:eatom", "angle:vatom").
failure_scenario: No numerical effect; the allocation is attributed to 'improper' in `info memory` / memory-usage output, which misleads anyone tracking KOKKOS memory.
suggested_fix: Change both tags to "angle:eatom" and "angle:vatom".

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and reallocated on every timestep on which per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of the reuse-and-zero pattern used by the other 13 styles in this group.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:74-87 (with the commented-out size check `//if(k_eatom.extent(0)<maxeatom) { // won't work without adding zero functor`), src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:74-83 and src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_kokkos.cpp:72-81 do an unconditional `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(...)` + `memoryKK->create_kokkos(...)`. The other styles solved the zeroing problem and reuse the buffer, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_class2xe_kokkos.cpp:74-80: `if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; d_eatom = ...; } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);`.
failure_scenario: No wrong results. With `compute pe/atom` or `compute stress/atom` active every output step triggers a device free+malloc of nmax (and 6*nmax) elements per angle style; on GPUs this serializes the step and can dominate the angle cost.
suggested_fix: Adopt the extent-check + Kokkos::deep_copy(...,0.0) pattern already used by angle_class2xe_kokkos.cpp and the other 13 styles in this group.

summary: The Kokkos thermostats remove/restore the velocity bias with the group-wide Compute::remove_bias_all()/_kk() hooks, but the CPU originals use the per-atom Compute::remove_bias(i,v[i]) - three bias-capable temperature computes implement only the per-atom form, so with 'fix_modify temp' pointing at one of them the /kk fix silently thermostats the biased velocities.
evidence: fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:135-143 and :158-166 'if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk(); else { ... temperature->remove_bias_all(); ... } }' (the identical pattern is at fix_temp_rescale_kokkos.cpp:138-146/161-169 and fix_temp_csvr_kokkos.cpp:129-137/158-166).  The CPU originals loop per atom: src/fix_temp_berendsen.cpp:183-193 'for (...) if (mask[i] & groupbit) { temperature->remove_bias(i,v[i]); v[i][0] *= lamda; ... temperature->restore_bias(i,v[i]); }' and src/fix_temp_rescale.cpp:183-191, src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_temp_csvr.cpp:48-57 of end_of_step.  src/compute.h:153-159 declares 'virtual void remove_bias_all() {}' / 'virtual void remove_bias_all_kk() {}' as empty base methods, and a scan of every compute that sets tempbias shows three that declare remove_bias(int,double*) but no remove_bias_all(): src/compute_temp_sphere.h:36-39, src/ASPHERE/compute_temp_asphere.h, src/BODY/compute_temp_body.h.  compute temp/sphere/kk (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:35 'kokkosable = 1') likewise overrides neither, so both the kk and the non-kk branch above are no-ops for it.
failure_scenario: 'compute ts all temp/sphere ... bias <some bias compute>' plus 'fix_modify 1 temp ts' on a 'fix temp/berendsen/kk' (or temp/rescale/kk, temp/csvr/kk): the bias is never subtracted, so the streaming/rotational component is rescaled together with the thermal one - the thermostat drives the wrong quantity, whereas the plain CPU fix removes the bias per atom.
suggested_fix: Either implement remove_bias_all()/restore_bias_all() (and the _kk variants) in compute temp/sphere, temp/asphere and temp/body, or make the /kk thermostats refuse a temperature compute whose remove_bias_all is the base no-op, as fix temp/csld/kk already does for the whole BIAS case (fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:103-104).

summary: Same defect as the lj/switch3 sibling: the Gaussian-charge Coulomb correction sits inside compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul, which pair_kokkos only calls when rsq < cut_coulsq, while the CPU base applies it whenever rsq < cut_ljsq[i][j].
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_mm3_switch3_coulgauss_long_kokkos.cpp:228-234 (`if (rsq < cut_ljsq_val && lj2_val > 0.0) { ... forcecoul += factor_coul*prefactor2*(erfc2+EWALD_F*rrij*expn2); }`) and :305-310 for the energy, both reachable only through src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:247-248/269-273 which gate on `rsq < d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)`. The CPU base src/YAFF/pair_mm3_switch3_coulgauss_long.cpp computes forcecoul2/erfc2/prefactor2 inside `if (rsq < cut_ljsq[itype][jtype])` (lines 83-103 of compute()) with no cut_coulsq test, and adds `ecoul += prefactor2*erfc2*factor_coul;` under the same cut_ljsq test (line 116); fpair at line 133 is `(forcecoul + factor_coul*forcecoul2 + factor_lj*forcelj)*r2inv`. cut_lj[i][j] may exceed cut_coul (init_one: `double cut = MAX(cut_lj[i][j],cut_coul+2.0*qdist);`, and pair_coeff takes an optional per-pair LJ cutoff).
failure_scenario: `pair_style mm3/switch3/coulgauss/long 10.0 8.0 3.0` (cut_lj 10, cut_coul 8): pairs at 8 <= r < 10 lose the -qqrd2e*qi*qj*erfc(gamma*r)/r Gaussian correction in both force and Coulomb energy relative to the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the Gaussian correction in compute_fpair/compute_evdwl (which are gated by cut_ljsq), or set d_cut_coulsq(i,j)/m_cut_coulsq[i][j] to max(cut_coulsq, cut_ljsq[i][j]) and gate the Ewald part on cut_coulsq inside compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul.

summary: compute_local() advances through the packed buffer with 'j += 2*numbonds + 3' without the store_bonds guard used everywhere else, so the stride would be wrong if it ever ran with store_bonds false.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.cpp:225 'j += 2*numbonds + 3;' vs the same walk in compute_bonds() at :184 'j += (store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3;' and compute_peratom() at :249 'j += (store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3;'. The packer only emits the bond entries under STORE_BONDS (src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4319-4335).
failure_scenario: Currently unreachable because ComputeReaxFFAtom sets 'local_flag = store_bonds' (src/REAXFF/compute_reaxff_atom.cpp:82), but a direct compute_local() call (library/Python interface, or a future caller) with 'bonds no' walks off the packed layout and reads garbage or past the buffer.
suggested_fix: Use the same '(store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3' stride in compute_local(), or assert store_bonds at its entry.

summary: Few's initializer_list constructor neither bounds-checks nor default-initializes: a list longer than n writes past the fixed buffer, a shorter one leaves elements uninitialized.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_few.h:113 'alignas(T) char array_[n * sizeof(T)];' and :117-122 'Few(std::initializer_list<T> l) { std::size_t i = 0; for (auto it = l.begin(); it != l.end(); ++it) { new (data() + (i++)) T(*it); } }'. There is no 'i < n' guard and no loop to construct the remaining n - l.size() elements, while the destructor at :132-134 unconditionally runs '(data()[i]).~T()' for all n. The sibling constructors at :124-130 correctly cover all n slots.
failure_scenario: 'Few<double,3> f = {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0};' constructs a fourth double past the end of array_ (stack/object corruption); 'Few<double,3> f = {1.0, 2.0};' leaves f[2] holding garbage that is then used as a coordinate or box length. No in-tree caller uses the initializer-list form today, so this is latent.
suggested_fix: Clamp the loop to n and default-construct the remaining slots, e.g. 'std::size_t i = 0; for (auto it = l.begin(); it != l.end() && i < n; ++it) new (data() + (i++)) T(*it); for (; i < n; ++i) new (data() + i) T();'.

summary: set_k_coeffelem() frees the previous coeffelem with memory->destroy(), which would corrupt the heap if it is ever called a second time on a model whose coeffelem is already Kokkos-backed.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_kokkos.h:87-100 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_coeffelem, tmp, model->nelements, model->nparams, ...); ... memory->destroy(model->coeffelem); model->coeffelem = tmp;'. After the first call model->coeffelem is the array produced by create_kokkos, whose row pointers alias Kokkos-owned memory (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:236-241 'array[i] = &data.view_host()(i,0);'), and the matching deallocator only frees the row-pointer block (memory_kokkos.h:272-281 destroy_kokkos, which does sfree(array) but never sfree(array[0])). Memory::destroy for a 2d array frees array[0] as well.
failure_scenario: Today the only callers are one-shot constructor paths (mliap_model_linear_kokkos.cpp:30, mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:81), so it does not fire; a second call (e.g. reloading coefficients for a deferred python model) would free Kokkos-owned memory with sfree() and corrupt the heap.
suggested_fix: Guard the swap, e.g. call memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_coeffelem, model->coeffelem) when k_coeffelem is already allocated, and only use memory->destroy() for the plain array from the first read_coeffs().

summary: pair sw/kk ignores the `threebody off` setting and always executes the O(jnum^2) three-body loop (results stay correct only because read_file zeroes lambda).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_sw_kokkos.cpp:418-422 `// there is no support for skipping threebody loops (yet) / bool tmp_threebody = skip_threebody_flag; skip_threebody_flag = false; PairSW::init_style(); skip_threebody_flag = tmp_threebody;` and compute() (lines 322-370) runs the jj/kk loop unconditionally, whereas src/MANYBODY/pair_sw.cpp:170-174 sets `jnumm1 = 0` when skip_threebody_flag. Numbers remain right only because src/MANYBODY/pair_sw.cpp:439 `if (skip_threebody_flag) params[nparams].lambda = 0;`.
failure_scenario: `pair_style sw/kk threebody off` runs the full three-body double loop with lambda=0, so sw/kk is several times slower than the CPU style for the same (two-body only) result.
suggested_fix: Guard the three-body loop with `if (!skip_threebody_flag)` (pass the flag into the functor), or at least skip the jj/kk loop when all lambda are zero.
